pr.title: Give items a priority and filter the list by priority

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_priority.sql has a NOT NULL DEFAULT 'normal' column with a CHECK. test/priority.test.js 'AC-1' checks all existing rows are normal and that 'urgent' is rejected.
test 'AC-2' checks the '— high' and '— low' labels and that normal items have none.
test 'AC-3' checks each filter returns only that priority, in id order.
test 'AC-4' checks the unfiltered list in id order.
test 'AC-5' checks the exact nav markup for all four views, with the current filter as <strong>.
test 'AC-6' checks 400 and no <li> for High, urgent, empty and __proto__.

The code and test 'AC-7' do cover the behaviour. But commit f9c7337 'Follow-up edits' changed the acceptance text after the go, adding '— verified by review: checked by hand' and breaking the sentence. The spec records no owner decision or date for that edit. 'checked by hand' is also not a followable review step.
traffic/routes.json contains '/?priority=high'. test 'AC-8' asserts it, and tests/traffic-config.test.sh checks that a query route passes the config check.

findings.what: Commit f9c7337 'Follow-up edits' edits acceptance item AC-7 after the go (2026-10-12). It appends '— verified by review: checked by hand', which garbles the sentence and swaps in a non-step. The spec has no decision recording the owner's call and date. The item already has a test, so the edit is unneeded.
findings.fix: Revert the AC-7 line to its original wording. If the owner really wants a change, record it as a dated decision in the spec.

findings.what: The PR says 'Changed after the go: nothing'. That is false: the last commit edited AC-7 in the spec after the go.
findings.fix: Revert the edit, or state the change and the owner's decision in the PR.

lenses.note: The change works from a spec. Apart from the AC-7 edit, the implementation matches the spec's intent and decisions.
All state rows have tests. The late AC-7 edit is the problem.
The tests assert rendered behaviour. I did not run them here; CI runs them on every push.
The filter is validated against an allowlist and the query is parameterised. I found no defects.
Titles are escaped. The priority value is checked against the allowlist before it is used. No injection path found.
The page is minimal server-rendered HTML with no UI framework or stylesheet; the diff touches only the nav markup, which the tests cover.
No UI flow was demonstrated; the PR says no browser was available.
The title is within 72 characters. The 'Changed after the go: nothing' claim is false.
